$comment: The browser stream's performance budgets, approved with the castd architecture (2026-11-19). Each is a one-directional claim a run is judged against with --compare; metric names are compare.ts's METRICS. 60 fps is judged as at least 57 unique frames a second, five percent short of the page's own rate, so one late frame is not a failure.

budgets.claim: A page that does not change costs the encoder nothing: no capture, no encode, until something moves.
Scrolling a page at 60 fps at about 1280x880 costs the encoder at most a fifth of a core.
A page scrolled at 60 fps is seen at 60 fps.
On a LAN, what the page drew is decoded within 40 ms for half the frames.
On a LAN, what the page drew is decoded within 60 ms for all but one frame in a hundred.
Over 10 Mbit/s with a 40 ms round trip, half the frames are decoded within 90 ms of being drawn.
Over 5 Mbit/s with a 60 ms round trip, a 60 Hz animation is still seen at 60 fps.
Over 5 Mbit/s with a 60 ms round trip, the picture never stands still for 100 ms while the page moves.
A keystroke's glyph is decoded within the link's round trip plus 30 ms, for half the keystrokes.
A 10,000-character paste is all on screen in under a second.
